quotes.text: I’ve built my career advocating for digital protections for our most vulnerable Americans, including children and seniors, from cyber threats like fraud, data breaches, deepfakes, and more. Businesses do better—and strive to do better—when commonsense laws are in place to guide their decisions. Trump's Executive Order fails to recognize the important role states play in shaping the policies that drive U.S. competitiveness and innovation. It could not be more clear: the Administration is actively seeking ways to make the internet a more dangerous place.

I had the pleasure of meeting with @pizzuro_john and Raven as they briefed Congressional offices on the current dangers of AI in child exploitation. As a former director of a nonprofit advocating for kids’ safety and well-being online, I am now focused on combating emerging threats to our children on @ScienceDems.

Congress must make active countermeasures against this dangerous activity in the rapidly evolving digital landscape.

It is deeply irresponsible and wholly absurd to force states to choose between expanding essential broadband infrastructure and protecting their residents—especially children and small businesses—from the growing and so far largely unchecked risks of artificial intelligence. [...] The inclusion of this moratorium puts children at greater risk of exposure to harmful content generated or amplified by AI, and it opens the door to unregulated copyright infringement that could devastate small creators and businesses.

This issue deserves a full, transparent debate and a stand-alone bill—not to be rammed through as a rider through our federal budget reconciliation process. I urge the Senate Majority to reconsider this misguided provision and put the priorities of families and businesses ahead of private tech interests.

As a former Deputy Assistant Secretary at the @NTIAgov, who oversaw the BEAD program and for decades worked to protect the safety of children online at @CommonSense, I fully condemn Senate Republicans’ inclusion of a provision that would force states to stop any AI regulation as a condition to expand broadband with federal funding in communities across the country. https://t.co/iuEq3GiLbL

Digital assets and AI are already shaping how we live and work from small business payments to food safety on farms. But with innovation can come risks.  That’s why I’m working to strengthen the bipartisan CLARITY Act with practical safeguards - my amendments close loopholes, require real conflict-of-interest rules, and ensure a level playing field for all market entrants.  Getting it right will ensure a more trust worthy financial eco-system.

This morning I joined @alivitali on MSNBC's @WayTooEarly to discuss the dangerous AI regulation moratorium in the House Majority-passed Budget Reconciliation Bill. Linking critical broadband funding — intended to close the digital divide, support rural communities, and provide lifesaving services — to the suppression of state-level AI oversight is both coercive and irresponsible. It forces states to choose between expanding internet access to better rural America and safeguarding their residents from potentially harmful and untested technologies.

I strongly urge my US Senate colleagues to reject this harmful moratorium on AI regulation and allow states to continue to invest in rural broadband as originally intended.

Join me on @msnbc @waytooearly at 5:40am as I discuss the serious risks of the Republicans’ AI regulation ban—and why expanding rural broadband is essential to creating jobs, improving health care and strengthening education access in my district and in communities across America. 

📺 Tune in!

States should NOT have to choose between expanding essential broadband infrastructure and protecting their residents—especially children and small businesses—from the rapidly evolving risks of artificial intelligence.

So I'm urging the Senate Majority to reject the 10-year AI moratorium within the budget package and insist on a transparent, stand-alone debate—because families and small businesses deserve better than backroom deals that serve Big Tech.

The BEAD program is about connecting every community not playing politics with public safety.

I joined my colleagues in urging the Senate to remove a reckless provision that would force states to give up their ability to regulate AI just to access broadband funding. That’s wrong.

We can close the digital divide and protect people from the risks of unregulated AI. We don’t have to choose and we shouldn’t have to. 
@DorisMatsui @RepGregLandsman @RepTroyCarter 

https://t.co/ggWYIdNniC

Freezing state and local AI safeguards is a step backwards for safe and dependable AI development. I was proud to join @DorisMatsui and lead 81 Members of Congress in making our stance clear: state-led, commonsense guardrails are key to ensuring AI works for American families, not against them.

I've made it my career to hold Big Tech accountable. In Congress, I'm fighting for legislation that puts responsible guardrails in the new AI economy and ensures companies are held accountable when consumers are harmed. This bill isn't the answer; we need stronger protections for states, consumers and families, not loopholes that let them operate unchecked.

https://t.co/A9Jyitywkp

As a mom of four and a longtime advocate for children’s online safety and well-being, it’s vital we study how artificial intelligence can impact our kids’ learning and development before it becomes embedded in their classrooms. While AI holds great potential, it also poses risks when its impact is not well vetted or understood. Our country owes it to our children to study how integrating AI in schools impacts them cognitively, socio-emotionally, and physically.

While Rep. Norman, a Freedom Caucus member, and I don’t often see “eye to eye”, I completely agree with him about the GOP’s horrific abdication of its congressional duties by canceling votes for the rest of September. We have so much to do on AI guardrails, making America more affordable, stopping corruption, helping our farmers and small businesses, and ending this war.

Biotechnology is not some distant future. It is here, and the countries that set the standards will lead it. At @axios  Live, I joined @caitlinnowens to discuss why AI needs trusted biological data and how my bipartisan SCALE Biology Act can move breakthroughs from the lab to patients.

I also toured an exhibit celebrating 50 years of Genentech innovation and the breakthroughs that have transformed patients’ lives.

Good. OpenAI saw serious safety concerns and hit the brakes. If only Republicans in Congress would stop stalling and move with the same urgency on real AI guardrails.

When AI can be used to develop bioweapons, Congress cannot afford to sit back.

I’m pushing for clear standards, early detection, and strong guardrails. We need to invest in our scientists and make safety a priority. Our health and national security depend on it. https://t.co/WBrK4ka0g9

Reports that AI industry leaders are preparing for the possibility of a catastrophic event within the next six to twelve months are deeply concerning. This is not a prediction set in stone—but it is a warning we cannot afford to ignore. If AI-enabled cyberattacks could disrupt our banks, internet, power, or water, then we must prepare before—not after—our critical systems are put at risk.

I have spent my career protecting people from cyber threats, fraud, data breaches, and other online harms. The promise of AI is enormous, but innovation cannot come at the expense of public safety. Congress must work with experts, industry, and federal agencies to test these systems, protect critical infrastructure, and hold developers accountable.

We can lead in AI without leaving Americans behind. The standard is simple: build boldly, but build responsibly—and always put people first.

Elon Musk’s companies rake in billions from taxpayer-funded government deals, and legitimize pay offs to Trump and his allies in the form of campaign donations.  Now Musk is pouring $276 million into keeping Republicans in power and corruptly stopping all safety guardrails on AI and Big Tech.  It’s not about US competitiveness or the American economy but rather the creation of a digital oligarchy that seeks to stop the ability of all Americans to democratize AI and build middle class prosperity. 

American families deserve a fair, transparent government which works for them and NOT one controlled by a self dealing trillionaire!

https://t.co/5DmlyLlSem

The Trump Administration’s FAA wants to take ownership positions in AI companies. That’s an insane and illegal conflict of interest! 

This Congress must exercise its Article 1 oversight powers with respect to any FAA ownership in private AI companies and demand answers about whether the systems being deployed at our airports have been adequately tested, are properly monitored, and are safe for the traveling public. 

This is exactly why I led a letter with @RepAOC, @RepDonBeyer, @RepSarahElfreth, @RepSuhas, and @RepKweisiMfume demanding answers from the FAA.  No insider dealing and no compromises on public transportation safety.

ICYMI: I’m leading the call with @RepAOC , @RepDonBeyer , @RepKweisiMfume, @RepSuhas, and @RepSarahElfreth to pause the FAA’s AI tool at DCA, Dulles, and BWI.

When Maryland families board a plane, they deserve to know the systems guiding their flight have been thoroughly tested and the people keeping them safe have the training they need.

After the devastating DCA crash that took 67 lives, the FAA owes this region answers. Show us the safety testing. Explain who is accountable if something goes wrong.

I support modernizing our aviation systems, but passenger safety must come first.
